title: Personal Credit Cards: using card points to restore an overdrawn autopay checking account
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: restoring an overdrawn autopay source with rewards points

This entry covers the Personal Credit Cards line of Piedmont Crescent Bank and is the invocation reference for restore_overdrawn_checking_with_points_4e4b44ef.

## What the policy governs

- **Situation:** a cardholder asks to apply rewards points to a card's balance while the PCB checking account named as that card's autopay source is overdrawn.
- **Handling:** the points needed to bring that checking account back to zero are redeemed as a deposit into that same checking account, because an overdrawn source cannot fund the autopay that pays the card.
- **Result it decides:** the number of points redeemed for that deposit.
- **Observable effect:** one deposit-to-checking redemption on the card naming that checking account as the receiving account, with the card's points reduced by the points redeemed.
- **Record kept:** this card policy records the redemption on the card only, as a redemption entry that names that checking account as the receiving account and carries the cash value. The matching entry on the checking account's own ledger is not posted by this card policy, and nothing in this policy reads or waits for it.

## How the tool is invoked

restore_overdrawn_checking_with_points_4e4b44ef is a customer-side tool. It must first be unlocked and handed over, to be run by the customer themselves: the agent unlocks it with unlock_user_discoverable_tool, and the customer themselves then runs it. The agent does not run it on the cardholder's behalf.

## What one call does

One call redeems rewards points from the cardholder's own credit card as a cash deposit into one of the cardholder's Piedmont Crescent Bank checking accounts. It posts one redemption entry on the card account for the number of points given, records the receiving checking account and the cash value delivered, and lowers the card's unredeemed points balance by those points at once. The redemption entry on the card, naming the receiving checking account, is the record of the deposit; the tool does not itself post an entry on the checking account's own ledger. The cardholder sees the points leave the card's rewards balance immediately, and the deposit described on the receipt. The tool books the values it is given and checks none of them.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| card_account_id | the reference number of the credit card account whose points are redeemed, as returned by the card account lookup | reference number text |
| checking_account_id | the reference number of the cardholder's checking account that receives the deposit, as returned by the checking account lookup | reference number text |
| reward_points | how many points are redeemed | a whole positive integer with no decimal part; never empty for this call |
| amount | the cash value delivered to the checking account | USD, a positive number rounded half-up to 2 decimal places; never empty for this call |

## Return

A text rendering of a dictionary with: status (always "redeemed" when the posting succeeded), card_txn_id (the new redemption entry), card_account_id, redemption_type (always deposit_to_checking), receiving_account_id (the checking account credited), reward_points (points redeemed), amount (USD, 2 decimal places), posted_date (YYYY-MM-DD, today) and new_rewards_balance (the card's unredeemed points afterwards). The call is complete when the receipt comes back with status "redeemed"; the tool defines no other outcome.
